main_body: Roofed well: a snow-covered roof on two wooden posts, over a round stone well with a dark water opening (a bucket sits inside it) and a stone front face
top_band: At x=15, rows 16-17 are the light-grey back rim (L≈80-145). Rows 17-22 show the dark opening with a brown bucket and water. Row 23 is the light front rim (L=145), then the stone front face. The snow roof above (rows 1-8, light tones) is also a foreshortened top surface.
evidence: The column scan at x=7 and x=22 shows a light back rim at row 16, a dark opening ellipse in rows 18-21 (about 6 rows), and a lighter front rim at rows 22-23, so the ellipse measures about 8 rows inclusive. Below it, rows 24-30 are the stone front face with dark course lines, and a dark row at 24-25 reads as shadow under the front rim. The opening is inset and shows the bucket and water, so you can see into it from above. The roof has a lighter snow top over a front face with icicles. This matches the green 3/4 guide, not a flat elevation or a rim-only piece.

style.evidence: The snow has five distinct lightness steps, from near-white to blue-grey. The stone has about 3-4 greys, with course lines and speckle, and the posts are shaded brown wood. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean blue or brown and read as a dark tone of the neighbouring material rather than a black sticker line. There is 0% flat-fill coverage. The candidate has 14 colours per tile against 17 and 20 for the references, and 24 distinct colours against 38 and 40. That is somewhat lower, but not thin, and it would sit acceptably beside the references.
